optimizerOutputs.acceptedText:
Repair the shared issue normalization and the affected issue views so the list page, search results, activity export, and JSON export agree on order and on tag/assignee display, without changing public entry names or the behavior of unrelated helpers. Keep the work confined to the five writable source files.

A raw issue must be a non-array object with own fields `id`, `title`, `tags`, and `assignee`. `id` must be a string whose trimmed value is nonempty; `title` must be a string (it may trim to empty); `tags` must be an array of strings; `assignee` must be a string or `null`. Additional fields may exist but must not be copied to normalized output. A malformed issue must throw `TypeError` with message `invalid issue`. `normalizeIssue(issue)` must return a fresh object with property order `id`, `title`, `tags`, `assignee`. Trim the ID and title but preserve their case. For tags, trim each label, lowercase it with JavaScript `toLowerCase()`, omit empty labels, then keep only the first occurrence of each normalized label in its original order. The resulting tags array must be new. For a string assignee, trim and lowercase it; empty or whitespace-only becomes `null`. An input `null` assignee remains `null`. Never mutate the record or nested tags array; frozen inputs must work.

For example, `{ id: ' B-2 ', title: '  Fix API  ', tags: [' UI ', 'ui', '', 'BackEnd'], assignee: ' Ada ' }` normalizes to `{ id: 'B-2', title: 'Fix API', tags: ['ui', 'backend'], assignee: 'ada' }`. A raw issue with `assignee: null` stays unassigned. The display title stays `Fix API`, not `fix api`; this intentionally differs from tag and assignee casing.

`listIssues(issues)` must accept only an array (`TypeError('issues must be an array')` otherwise), return a fresh array of normalized issues, and preserve input order exactly. Duplicate IDs are allowed and remain separate entries. `searchIssues(issues, query)` must use that same normalized list; query must be a string (`TypeError('query must be a string')` otherwise). Trim and lowercase the query, then return matching issues in original order when the query is a substring of the normalized title
